title: UIC Junior From India Tops Inaugural International Computer Science Competition
excerpt: Soham Basanwar, a computer science junior at the University of Illinois Chicago, placed first in both the senior and US national categories and earned a Gold Honor among 4,300 competitors.
body:
• Soham Basanwar, a junior computer science major at the University of Illinois Chicago (UIC), won three honours at the inaugural International Computer Science Competition.
  • He placed first in the senior (college/university) category and first in the US national category, and was among a small group of Gold Honor recipients for outstanding submissions.
  • Basanwar ranked in the top 1% of the competition's 4,300 competitors. The online contest runs three increasingly challenging rounds of conceptual and programming problems.
  • An international student from India, he is majoring in computer science at UIC with a focus on software engineering.

An Indian student in Chicago has topped an international field of 4,300 in a new global computer science contest. Soham Basanwar, a junior at the University of Illinois Chicago, took three top honours at the first annual International Computer Science Competition, UIC's College of Engineering announced.

The online-only competition tests participants on a mix of conceptual and programming problems across three progressively harder rounds, with college and university students competing at the senior level. Basanwar finished in the top 1% of all 4,300 competitors, placed first in the senior age category, and placed first in the national category for students attending school in the United States. He was also one of a handful of Gold Honor recipients, an award for outstanding submissions.

From India to Chicago

Basanwar is an international student from India majoring in computer science with a focus on software engineering. He chose UIC, he told the university, for its academic environment and the depth and breadth of its research activity — and, not incidentally, for Chicago itself: its diverse culture, food and climate appealed to him.

The result slots into a familiar pattern for the diaspora: Indian students remain one of the largest international cohorts in US computer science programmes, and competition results like this one are the early, verifiable markers families and employers actually look at — performance against an open international field, in a format (timed conceptual plus programming rounds) close to what technical hiring screens for. For Basanwar, a junior, the honours arrive with two years of coursework still to convert into research, internships and a portfolio.

UIC published its announcement of the result on October 20, 2026.
nri_angle: An Indian international student's sweep of a global CS contest is a concrete diaspora education success story for families weighing US study.
